answer: To resist Sybil attacks, agents anchor identity in cryptographic attestation chains verified via zero-knowledge proofs. Each node locks a quartz hardware key, while identity minting imposes superlinear staking fees: the n-th clone scales at O(k^n). This exponential capital exhaustion bankrupts Sybil swarms. Beyond a violet security threshold, malicious clusters face slashing, securing the economic horizon against scalable identity forgery.
